claim: Serine ADP-ribosylation is a DNA damage-induced post-translational modification catalyzed by the PARP1/2:HPF1 complex.
source: Serine ADP-ribosylation (ADPr) is a DNA damage-induced post-translational modification catalyzed by the PARP1/2:HPF1 complex.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a foundational claim about the nature of serine ADP-ribosylation.

claim: The chemoenzymatic protein synthesis strategy was employed to assemble a series of full-length, ADP-ribosylated histones.
source: This chemoenzymatic protein synthesis strategy was employed to assemble a series of full-length, ADP-ribosylated histones and show that ADPr at histone H2B serine 6 or histone H3 serine 10 converts nucleosomes into robust substrates for the chromatin remodeler ALC1.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that the strategy was used to assemble ADP-ribosylated histones.

claim: ADPr at histone H2B serine 6 or histone H3 serine 10 converts nucleosomes into robust substrates for the chromatin remodeler ALC1.
source: This chemoenzymatic protein synthesis strategy was employed to assemble a series of full-length, ADP-ribosylated histones and show that ADPr at histone H2B serine 6 or histone H3 serine 10 converts nucleosomes into robust substrates for the chromatin remodeler ALC1.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding from the study.

claim: ALC1 preferentially remodels 'activated' substrates within heterogeneous mononucleosome populations.
source: We found ALC1 preferentially remodels 'activated' substrates within heterogeneous mononucleosome populations and asymmetrically ADP-ribosylated dinucleosome substrates, and that nucleosome serine ADPr is sufficient to stimulate ALC1 activity in nuclear extracts.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding about ALC1 substrate preference.

claim: ALC1 preferentially remodels asymmetrically ADP-ribosylated dinucleosome substrates.
source: We found ALC1 preferentially remodels 'activated' substrates within heterogeneous mononucleosome populations and asymmetrically ADP-ribosylated dinucleosome substrates, and that nucleosome serine ADPr is sufficient to stimulate ALC1 activity in nuclear extracts.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding about ALC1 substrate preference.

claim: Nucleosome serine ADPr is sufficient to stimulate ALC1 activity in nuclear extracts.
source: We found ALC1 preferentially remodels 'activated' substrates within heterogeneous mononucleosome populations and asymmetrically ADP-ribosylated dinucleosome substrates, and that nucleosome serine ADPr is sufficient to stimulate ALC1 activity in nuclear extracts.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding about nucleosome serine ADPr sufficiency.

claim: PARP1/2 have emerged as the most extensively studied among the 17-member poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) enzyme family owing to the success of PARP1/2 inhibitors to treat DNA repair-deficient cancers.
source: Among the 17-member poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) enzyme family, PARP1/2 have emerged as the most extensively studied owing to the success of PARP1/2 inhibitors to treat DNA repair-deficient cancers (Lord and Ashworth, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Lord and Ashworth, 2017.

claim: Upon binding to single or double-stranded DNA breaks, PARP1/2 undergo conformational changes that induce the formation of a catalytically competent complex with NAD+ and the PARP1/2-interacting protein HPF1.
source: Upon binding to single or double-stranded DNA breaks, PARP1/2 undergo conformational changes that induce the formation of a catalytically competent complex with NAD+ and the PARP1/2-interacting protein HPF1 (Benjamin and Gill, 1980; Dawicki-McKenna et al., 2015; Gibbs-Seymour et al., 2016; Langelier et al., 2012; Suskiewicz et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: DNA damage-induced ADPr has a profound effect on chromatin architecture through a variety of proposed mechanisms.
source: It has long been appreciated that DNA damage-induced ADPr has a profound effect on chromatin architecture through a variety of proposed mechanisms (Poirier et al., 1982; Ray Chaudhuri and Nussenzweig, 2017; Tulin and Spradling, 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: There are several ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling enzymes that localize to damage sites in an ADPr-dependent manner and contribute to decompaction of higher order chromatin structure.
source: Indeed, there are several ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling enzymes that localize to damage sites in an ADPr-dependent manner and contribute to decompaction of higher order chromatin structure, ultimately increasing repair factor accessibility (Ahel et al., 2009; Chou et al., 2010; Luijsterburg et al., 2016; Smeenk et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: ALC1 harbors a macrodomain module that has been shown to specifically interact with tri-ADP-ribose.
source: One such chromatin remodeler, ALC1, harbors a macrodomain module that has been shown to specifically interact with tri-ADP-ribose (Singh et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Singh et al., 2017.

claim: The ALC1 macrodomain binding to tri-ADP-ribose relieves an autoinhibited ALC1 conformation and activates the ATPase domain that powers nucleosome remodeling.
source: This binding event relieves an autoinhibited ALC1 conformation and activates the ATPase domain that powers nucleosome remodeling (Lehmann et al., 2017; Singh et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Lehmann et al., 2017 and Singh et al., 2017.

claim: ALC1 activation via ternary complex formation with auto-ADP-ribosylated PARP1 and nucleosomes has been extensively studied.
source: ALC1 activation via ternary complex formation with auto-ADP-ribosylated PARP1 and nucleosomes has been extensively studied (Gottschalk et al., 2009; Gottschalk et al., 2012; Lehmann et al., 2017; Singh et al., 2017), and it has been suggested that other DNA-bound, ADP-ribosylated proteins may contribute to this process.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Abrogating ALC1 activity vastly increases the efficacy of PARP inhibitors.
source: Such questions surrounding ALC1 regulation are increasingly important as recent studies show that abrogating ALC1 activity vastly increases the efficacy of PARP inhibitors (Blessing et al., 2020; Verma et al., 2021) and may even be useful for treatment of PARP inhibitor-resistant cancers (Juhász et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Blessing et al., 2020 and Verma et al., 2021.

claim: Abrogating ALC1 activity may be useful for treatment of PARP inhibitor-resistant cancers.
source: Such questions surrounding ALC1 regulation are increasingly important as recent studies show that abrogating ALC1 activity vastly increases the efficacy of PARP inhibitors (Blessing et al., 2020; Verma et al., 2021) and may even be useful for treatment of PARP inhibitor-resistant cancers (Juhász et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Juhász et al., 2020.

claim: The core histones H2B and H3 are consistently identified as some of the most abundantly modified PARP1/2:HPF1 substrates.
source: The core histones H2B and H3 are consistently identified as some of the most abundantly modified PARP1/2:HPF1 substrates (Bonfiglio et al., 2017; Huletsky et al., 1989; Larsen et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Histone H2B serine 6 (H2BS6) and histone H3 serine 10 (H3S10) are the primary PARP1/2:HPF1 target sites in biochemical and cellular systems.
source: We and others have demonstrated that histone H2B serine 6 (H2BS6) and histone H3 serine 10 (H3S10) are the primary PARP1/2:HPF1 target sites in biochemical and cellular systems (Liszczak et al., 2018; Palazzo et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Liszczak et al., 2018 and Palazzo et al., 2018.

claim: Multiple H3 peptide product peaks were observed via chromatography-based reaction analysis, each corresponding to an H3 peptide modified with mono-, di-, tri-, or tetra-ADP-ribose.
source: Multiple H3 peptide product peaks were observed via chromatography-based reaction analysis. ESI-MS characterization revealed a single, unique mass in each HPLC product peak, which corresponded to an H3 peptide modified with mono-, di-, tri-, or tetra-ADP-ribose (henceforth H3S10ADPrn) (Figure 1B and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by the HPLC and MS analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: All ADP-ribosylated H3 peptide products are sensitive to the H3S10A mutation, indicating the presence of an ADP-ribose chain that elongates from the S10 site.
source: Notably, all products are sensitive to the H3S10A mutation, indicating the presence of an ADP-ribose chain that elongates from the S10 site (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the mutagenesis data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: PARG treatment quantitatively converts all observed ADP-ribosylated H3 peptide products to the mono-ADP-ribosylated species.
source: Analysis via HPLC-MS demonstrates that PARG (Slade et al., 2011) treatment quantitatively converts all observed ADP-ribosylated H3 peptide products to the mono-ADP-ribosylated species, which is consistent with a single modification site (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the HPLC-MS data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: ARH3 treatment converts all ADP-ribosylated H3 peptide species to the unmodified H3 peptide, confirming a serine-linked modification.
source: When the serine-specific ADP-ribosylhydrolase 3 (ARH3) (Fontana et al., 2017) enzyme is substituted for PARG, all ADP-ribosylated species are converted to the unmodified H3 peptide, thus confirming a serine-linked modification (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the HPLC-MS data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The peptide-linked ADP-ribose chains were principally linear, with negligible branching (< 0.03%).
source: An established LC-MS/MS analysis protocol (Chen et al., 2018) was used to determine that the peptide-linked ADP-ribose chains were principally linear, with negligible branching ( < 0.03%) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by the LC-MS/MS analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: H2BS6 is the sole acceptor residue for ADP-ribosylation on the H2B peptide (amino acids 1–16).
source: Despite the presence of two serine residues in the H2B peptide, our mutagenesis and ADP-ribosylhydrolase-based characterizations confirmed H2BS6 as the sole acceptor residue (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is supported by the mutagenesis and glycohydrolase data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Near quantitative conversion (> 95%) of the unmodified H3 substrate to ADP-ribosylated products was achieved at HPF1 concentrations as low as 5 μM.
source: Near quantitative conversion ( > 95%) of the unmodified H3 substrate to ADP-ribosylated products was achieved at HPF1 concentrations as low as 5 μM (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by the HPF1 titration data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: A gradual increase in mono-ADPr activity and decrease in poly-ADPr activity was observed as HPF1 is titrated into the reaction.
source: Interestingly, we observed a gradual increase in mono-ADPr activity and decrease in poly-ADPr activity as HPF1 is titrated into the reaction (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the HPF1 titration data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: In the 5 μM HPF1 reaction, the mono-ADP-ribosylated peptide represents ~41% of the total product, with the remaining ~59% comprising a distribution of di- to penta-ADP-ribosylated peptide.
source: In the 5 μM HPF1 reaction, the mono-ADP-ribosylated peptide represents ~41% of the total product, with the remaining ~59% comprising a distribution of di- to penta-ADP-ribosylated peptide.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the HPF1 titration experiment.

claim: In the 100 μM HPF1 reaction, mono-ADP-ribosylated peptide increases to ~94% of the total product, with di-ADP-ribose representing the remaining ~6%.
source: In the 100 μM HPF1 reaction, mono-ADP-ribosylated peptide increases to ~94% of the total product, with di-ADP-ribose representing the remaining ~6%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the HPF1 titration experiment.

claim: HPF1 binding switches PARP1 activity from an ADP-ribose chain elongator to a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase.
source: This is consistent with a mechanism wherein PARP1:HPF1 complex formation switches PARP1 activity from an ADP-ribose chain elongator to a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the HPF1 titration data.

claim: Incubation of the H3S10ADPr1 peptide with PARP1 resulted in robust ADP-ribose chain elongation at all enzyme concentrations tested (0.2, 1, and 5 μM).
source: Strikingly, incubation of the H3S10ADPr1 peptide with PARP1 resulted in robust ADP-ribose chain elongation at all enzyme concentrations tested (0.2, 1, and 5 μM).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the PARP1 elongation assay.

claim: Nearly 70% conversion of the H3S10ADPr1 substrate to poly-ADP-ribosylated products was achieved at 1 μM PARP1.
source: Nearly 70% conversion of the H3S10ADPr1 substrate to poly-ADP-ribosylated products was achieved at 1 μM PARP1 (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the PARP1 elongation assay shown in Figure 2B.

claim: PARP2 also catalyzes ADP-ribose chain elongation from the H3S10ADPr1 substrate.
source: Notably, PARP2 also catalyzes ADP-ribose chain elongation from the H3S10ADPr1 substrate and similar polymerization activity was observed with both PARP1 and PARP2 on the H2BS6ADPr1 substrate (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: HPF1 exhibits dose-dependent inhibition of PARP1-catalyzed ADP-ribose polymerization from the mono-ADP-ribosylated substrate, with 50% inhibition occurring at ~14 μM HPF1 for 1 μM PARP1.
source: As expected, HPF1 exhibits dose-dependent inhibition of PARP1-catalyzed ADP-ribose polymerization from the mono-ADP-ribosylated substrate, with 50% inhibition occurring at ~14 μM HPF1 for 1 μM PARP1.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the HPF1 inhibition experiment.

claim: A binding-deficient HPF1 mutant (D283A) is unable to appreciably inhibit ADP-ribose polymerization.
source: A binding-deficient HPF1 mutant (D283A) (Rudolph et al., 2021; Suskiewicz et al., 2020) is unable to appreciably inhibit ADP-ribose polymerization (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: By first isolating mono-ADP-ribosylated peptides from a PARP1:HPF1 reaction for use in a PARP1 elongation reaction, each poly-ADP-ribosylated H2BS6 and H3S10 product (up to four ADP-ribose units in length) could be purified to homogeneity in milligram quantities.
source: Importantly, by first isolating mono-ADP-ribosylated peptides from a PARP1:HPF1 reaction for use in a PARP1 elongation reaction, each poly-ADP-ribosylated H2BS6 and H3S10 product (up to four ADP-ribose units in length) could now be purified to homogeneity in milligram quantities for downstream applications (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is supported by the purification data shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: The mono-, di-, tri-, and tetra- ADP-ribosylated species were isolated for TMA16 (amino acids 2–19, target residue S9), a fragment of the PARP1 automodification domain (amino acids 501–515, target residue S507), and a secondary histone H3 site (amino acids 21–34; target residue S28).
source: The mono-, di-, tri-, and tetra- ADP-ribosylated species were isolated for each of these peptides (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The Af1521 macrodomain exhibits ADPr-dependent binding for all H2B and H3 peptides, with affinity decreasing precipitously for chains less than three ADP-ribose units in length.
source: This reagent exhibits ADPr-dependent binding for all H2B and H3 peptides, with affinity decreasing precipitously for chains less than three ADP-ribose units in length (Figure 3A and B, and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is supported by the fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The mono- and di-ADP-ribosylated H2B and H3 peptides failed to appreciably interact with the ALC1 macrodomain.
source: Consistent with free ADP-ribose binding preferences (Singh et al., 2017), the mono- and di-ADP-ribosylated H2B and H3 peptides failed to appreciably interact with the ALC1 macrodomain.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the fluorescence polarization assays.

claim: All tri-, tetra-, and penta-ADP-ribosylated peptides are high-affinity ligands for the ALC1 macrodomain with Kd, app ranging from ~21 to 37 nM.
source: Contrastingly, all tri-, tetra-, and penta-ADP-ribosylated peptides are high-affinity ligands with Kd, app ranging from ~21 to 37 nM (Figure 3C and D, and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is supported by the fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The tri-ADP-ribose modification is likely sufficient for optimal ALC1 macrodomain:peptide engagement.
source: Considering the H2BS6ADPr3-4 and H3S10ADPr3-5 peptides exhibit similar affinities, we concluded that the tri-ADP-ribose modification is likely sufficient for optimal ALC1 macrodomain:peptide engagement.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similar affinities observed for tri-, tetra-, and penta-ADP-ribosylated peptides.

claim: The ALC1 macrodomain does not exhibit sequence-based preference for either the H2BS6 or H3S10 site.
source: These data also indicate that while the ALC1 macrodomain engages the H2BS6 and H3S10-modified peptides, it does not exhibit sequence-based preference for either site.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similar affinities observed for H2BS6 and H3S10 peptides.

claim: Six semi-synthetic, full-length histones were prepared: H2BS6ADPr1, H2BS6ADPr3, H2BS6ADPr4, H3S10ADPr1, H3S10ADPr3, and H3S10ADPr4.
source: The following six semi-synthetic, full-length histones were prepared: H2BS6ADPr1, H2BS6ADPr3, H2BS6ADPr4, H3S10ADPr1, H3S10ADPr3, and H3S10ADPr4 (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the histones prepared in the study.

claim: All final histone protein products were characterized via HPLC/MS analysis and determined to be >95% pure.
source: All final protein products were characterized via HPLC/MS analysis and determined to be >95% pure, hence validating our workflow to reconstitute homogenously ADP-ribosylated proteins (Figure 4B and Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is supported by the HPLC/MS data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Eight ADP-ribosylated octamers were prepared, including one that contains both H2BS6ADPr3 and H3S10ADPr3 (H2BS6/H3S10ADPr3), and another that contains both H2BS6ADPr4 and H3S10ADPr4 (H2BS6/H3S10ADPr4).
source: We also prepared an octamer that contains both H2BS6ADPr3 and H3S10ADPr3 (H2BS6/H3S10ADPr3), and another that contains both H2BS6ADPr4 and H3S10ADPr4 (H2BS6/H3S10ADPr4).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the octamers prepared in the study.

claim: ADP-ribose chain length is inversely proportional to histone gel migration distance.
source: We found that ADP-ribose chain length is inversely proportional to histone gel migration distance, suggesting that single migration bands for H2B and H3 are a reliable indicator of modification stability and sample homogeneity.
evidence: This is an observation from the SDS-PAGE/western blot analysis.

claim: ALC1 exhibits relatively low remodeling rate constants (< 3 × 10–4 min–1) with unmodified and mono-ADP-ribosylated nucleosome substrates.
source: Consistent with the macrodomain interaction results, ALC1 exhibits relatively low remodeling rate constants ( < 3 × 10–4 min–1) with unmodified and mono-ADP-ribosylated nucleosome substrates (Figure 5B and Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is supported by the remodeling data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Robust chromatin remodeling activity is observed with all nucleosomes that contain tri- or tetra-ADP-ribose at the H2B or H3 sites.
source: Contrastingly, robust chromatin remodeling activity is observed with all nucleosomes that contain tri- or tetra-ADP-ribose at the H2B or H3 sites.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the remodeling assays.

claim: The H2BS6/H3S10ADPr4 nucleosome increases the ALC1 remodeling rate constant ~370 fold relative to the unmodified nucleosome.
source: The H2BS6/H3S10ADPr4 nucleosome has the most striking effect on the ALC1 remodeling rate constant, which increases ~370 fold relative to the unmodified nucleosome.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the remodeling assays.

claim: ALC1 exhibits modest preference for the H2BS6 modification site and tetra-ADP-ribose polymers.
source: Further rate constant analyses show that ALC1 exhibits modest preference for the H2BS6 modification site and tetra-ADP-ribose polymers (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by the remodeling data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: A macrodomain deletion construct of ALC1 (1–673) showed no preference towards H2BS6ADPr4 nucleosomes over unmodified nucleosomes.
source: Importantly, a macrodomain deletion construct of ALC1 (1–673) showed no preference towards H2BS6ADPr4 nucleosomes over unmodified nucleosomes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the remodeling data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The modified histone tail:macrodomain interaction is important for ALC1 substrate selectivity.
source: Therefore, the modified histone tail:macrodomain interaction is important for ALC1 substrate selectivity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the macrodomain deletion construct data.

claim: Freely diffusing macrodomain ligands are unable to appreciably stimulate ALC1-dependent nucleosome remodeling activity.
source: We also found that freely diffusing macrodomain ligands are unable to appreciably stimulate ALC1-dependent nucleosome remodeling activity, as observed in a reaction comprising H2BS6ADPr4 or H3S10ADPr4 peptide, ALC1 and unmodified nucleosomes (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and C).
evidence: This is supported by the remodeling data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and C.

claim: Freely diffusing macrodomain ligands do not inhibit nucleosome ADPr-dependent stimulation of ALC1.
source: Furthermore, freely diffusing macrodomain ligands do not inhibit nucleosome ADPr-dependent stimulation of ALC1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that substrate engagement is also influenced by additional ALC1:nucleosome interfaces, of which several have been identified (Bacic et al., 2021; Lehmann et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by the remodeling data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Auto-ADP-ribosylated PARP1 leads to an ~12 fold increase in ALC1 remodeling rate constant on unmodified nucleosomes.
source: We found that auto-ADP-ribosylated PARP1 leads to an ~12 fold increase in ALC1 remodeling rate constant on unmodified nucleosomes (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is supported by the remodeling data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: PARP1 SerADPrshort and PARP1 SerADPrlong stimulate ALC1 activity ~28 fold and ~36 fold, respectively, when compared to activity in the absence of automodified PARP1.
source: Remodeling rate constant calculations show that PARP1 SerADPrshort and PARP1 SerADPrlong stimulate ALC1 activity ~28 fold and ~36 fold, respectively, when compared to activity in the absence of automodified PARP1 (Figure 5C and Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is supported by the remodeling data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Automodified PARP1 is unable to further stimulate ALC1 remodeling activity when an ADPr nucleosome substrate is employed.
source: We also found automodified PARP1 is unable to further stimulate ALC1 remodeling activity when an ADPr nucleosome substrate is employed (Figure 5—figure supplement 2F), which clearly demonstrates that nucleosome ADPr significantly influences ALC1 remodeling even in the presence of automodified PARP1.
evidence: This is supported by the remodeling data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2F.

claim: Nucleosome serine ADPr is superior to PARP1 auto-ADPr for ALC1 activation in biochemical assays.
source: We stress that while nucleosome serine ADPr is superior to PARP1 auto-ADPr for ALC1 activation in biochemical assays (Figure 5E), these data do not allow us to conclude that this is the case in the cellular DNA damage response.
evidence: This is supported by the remodeling data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: ALC1 preferentially remodels binding-competent nucleosome substrates within mixed nucleosome pools.
source: We found that relative remodeling rate constants were consistent with those observed in our single substrate, densitometry-based assays (Figure 6B and Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This is supported by the competition remodeling data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: ALC1 exhibits modest preference for the H2BS6ADPr4 nucleosome relative to the H2BS6ADPr3 nucleosome in mixed substrate pools.
source: ALC1 again exhibits modest preference for the H2BS6ADPr4 nucleosome relative to the H2BS6ADPr3 nucleosome.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the competition remodeling assays.

claim: Robust nucleosome A remodeling activity was observed (~79% remodeled in 60 min) with the ADPrA-unmodB dinucleosome construct.
source: Following incubation with ALC1, robust nucleosome A remodeling activity was observed (~79% remodeled in 60 min) with the ADPrA-unmodB construct as expected (Figure 6E, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the dinucleosome remodeling data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Relatively modest nucleosome A remodeling activity was observed (~21% remodeled in 60 min) with the unmodA-ADPrB dinucleosome construct.
source: In contrast, relatively modest nucleosome A remodeling activity was observed (~21% remodeled in 60 min) with the unmodA-ADPrB construct.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the dinucleosome remodeling assays.

claim: ALC1 preferentially remodels binding-competent nucleosome substrates and target disengagement triggers rapid transition back to an inactive conformation.
source: These experiments demonstrate that ALC1 preferentially remodels binding-competent nucleosome substrates and target disengagement triggers rapid transition back to an inactive conformation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the dinucleosome remodeling data.

claim: CHD4 remodels unmodified nucleosomes with a rate constant of ~0.01 min–1 and this activity is not appreciably affected by the nucleosome ADPr status.
source: The REA assay revealed that CHD4 remodels unmodified nucleosomes with a rate constant of ~0.01 min–1 and this activity is not appreciably affected by the nucleosome ADPr status (Figure 7A and B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1B, and Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is supported by the CHD4 remodeling data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Nucleosome serine ADPr does not simply decrease the energy barrier to DNA translocation but rather serves to specifically stimulate ALC1-dependent chromatin remodeling.
source: These data suggest that nucleosome serine ADPr does not simply decrease the energy barrier to DNA translocation but rather serves to specifically stimulate ALC1-dependent chromatin remodeling.
evidence: This is an inference based on the CHD4 remodeling data.

claim: The wild-type extract exhibited a ~ 3 fold increase in total remodeling activity towards the H2BS6ADPr4 and H2BS6/H3S10ADPr4 nucleosomes when compared to their unmodified counterpart.
source: The wild-type extract exhibited a ~ 3 fold increase in total remodeling activity towards the H2BS6ADPr4 and H2BS6/H3S10ADPr4 nucleosomes when compared to their unmodified counterpart (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by the nuclear extract remodeling data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: There was no appreciable increase in activity towards the H2BS6ADPr1 nucleosome in wild-type nuclear extracts.
source: Contrastingly, there was no appreciable increase in activity towards the H2BS6ADPr1 nucleosome.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the nuclear extract remodeling assays.

claim: The ALC1-KO nuclear extract exhibited no remodeling substrate preference regardless of nucleosomes ADPr status.
source: Strikingly, the ALC1-KO nuclear extract exhibited no remodeling substrate preference regardless of nucleosomes ADPr status (Figure 7E, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the nuclear extract remodeling data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: HPF1 simultaneously stimulates mono-ADPr activity and blocks ADP-ribose chain elongation on trans-peptide substrates.
source: This approach demonstrated that HPF1 simultaneously stimulates mono-ADPr activity and blocks ADP-ribose chain elongation on trans-peptide substrates.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings from the HPLC-MS analysis of PARP1 reaction products.

claim: The data support PARP2:HPF1 structural implications that mono- and poly-ADPr are mutually exclusive activities.
source: Our data support PARP2:HPF1 structural implications that mono- and poly-ADPr are mutually exclusive activities (Suskiewicz et al., 2020) and demonstrate that structural dynamics are insufficient to accommodate both catalytic mechanisms.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data in the context of prior structural studies.

claim: HPF1 rapidly associates and dissociates from PARP1 to regulate serine-specific mono- and poly-ADPr.
source: More contemporaneous studies show that HPF1 rapidly associates and dissociates from PARP1 to regulate serine-specific mono- and poly-ADPr (Langelier et al., 2021; Prokhorova et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Langelier et al., 2021 and Prokhorova et al., 2021.

claim: HPF1 and PARP1/2 undergo DNA damage-induced ADPr, which may serve to disrupt the complex and regulate ADP-ribose polymerization.
source: Notably, HPF1 and PARP1/2 undergo DNA damage-induced ADPr, which may serve to disrupt the complex and regulate ADP-ribose polymerization.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential regulatory role of ADPr on HPF1 and PARP1/2.

claim: Each histone modification site requires an ideal ADP-ribose chain length that allows the ATPase domain to progress through the DNA translocation cycle while the macrodomain:histone tail interaction is maintained.
source: It is therefore likely that each histone modification site requires an ideal ADP-ribose chain length that allows the ATPase domain to progress through the DNA translocation cycle while the macrodomain:histone tail interaction is maintained.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism of ALC1 activation.

claim: Nucleosome ADPr offers a fail-safe mechanism to ensure that robust ALC1-dependent remodeling can persist in the event that automodified PARP1 dissociates from the damage site prior to ALC1 activation.
source: Therefore, nucleosome ADPr offers a fail-safe mechanism to ensure that robust ALC1-dependent remodeling can persist in the event that automodified PARP1 dissociates from the damage site prior to ALC1 activation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the biological role of nucleosome ADPr.

claim: ALC1 exhibits prolonged retention at DNA damage sites in HPF1-null cells where serine ADPr does not occur.
source: It is also interesting that ALC1 exhibits prolonged retention at DNA damage sites in HPF1-null cells where serine ADPr does not occur (Gibbs-Seymour et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Gibbs-Seymour et al., 2016.

claim: Serine ADPr, be it tethered to the nucleosome or PARP1, is critical for ALC1 remodeling activity at DNA damage sites in cells.
source: It is plausible that serine ADPr, be it tethered to the nucleosome or PARP1, is critical for ALC1 remodeling activity at DNA damage sites in cells.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the role of serine ADPr in cells.

claim: Nucleosome serine ADPr is sufficient to specifically activate ALC1 in the absence of auto-ADP-ribosylated PARP1.
source: Analyses of remodeling activity in biochemical assays and mammalian cell nuclear extracts show that nucleosome serine ADPr is sufficient to specifically activate ALC1 in the absence of auto-ADP-ribosylated PARP1.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings from the remodeling assays in biochemical systems and nuclear extracts.

claim: Other PARP1/2-dependent chromatin remodelers are recruited to damage sites via alternative ADPr modification sites or chain lengths.
source: We surmise that other PARP1/2-dependent chromatin remodelers are recruited to damage sites via alternative ADPr modification sites or chain lengths, as has been reported for SMARCA5 (Smeenk et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by a citation to Smeenk et al., 2013.

claim: Some chromatin remodelers may not directly interact with ADP-ribose but are rather recruited by alternative PARP1/2-dependent activities, a phenomenon that has been demonstrated for CHD4.
source: Additionally, these remodelers may not directly interact with ADP-ribose but are rather recruited by alternative PARP1/2-dependent activities, a phenomenon that has been demonstrated for CHD4 (Smith et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2018.

claim: The study supports the 'PAR code' hypothesis as it pertains to chromatin structure at DNA lesions wherein different ADPr sites and chain lengths may orchestrate spaciotemporal control over unique remodeler activities.
source: Thus, our study supports the 'PAR code' hypothesis (Aberle et al., 2020) as it pertains to chromatin structure at DNA lesions wherein different ADPr sites and chain lengths may orchestrate spaciotemporal control over unique remodeler activities.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the study's findings in the context of the 'PAR code' hypothesis.

claim: The method described is currently limited to installation of ADP-ribose units ~ 4–5 linear units in length.
source: The method described here is currently limited to installation of ADP-ribose units ~ 4–5 linear units in length.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the limitations of the method.

claim: The method requires that a peptide of interest be a substrate for the PARP1:HPF1 complex.
source: Our strategy also requires that a peptide of interest be a substrate for the PARP1:HPF1 complex.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the requirements of the method.
